test_title: PYST 79: SSC CGL 2024 - General Knowledge (Held On 26 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The Gandak river is a tributary of which river?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganga river**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gandak river is a significant tributary of the Ganga river.
 
• It originates in the Himalayas in Nepal and flows through the Indian states of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh before joining the Ganga.
 
• The river is known as Narayani in its upper reaches in Nepal.
 
• The Gandak river basin is an important agricultural area in the region, providing water for irrigation and supporting a large population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ganga River**

 
 
• The Ganga is one of the major rivers of the Indian subcontinent, flowing through the northern plains of India and Bangladesh.
 
• It is considered sacred in Hinduism and is worshipped as the goddess Ganga.
 
• The river has a length of about 2,525 kilometers (1,569 miles).
 
• The Ganga river basin is the most populous basin in the world, supporting hundreds of millions of people who rely on it for their water needs.
 
 
 
• **Yamuna River**
 
 
• The Yamuna is the second-largest tributary river of the Ganga in northern India.
 
• It originates from the Yamunotri Glacier in the Himalayas and flows through several states including Uttarakhand, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Delhi.
 
• The river meets the Ganga at the Triveni Sangam in Allahabad (Prayagraj).
 
 
 
• **Kaveri River**
 
 
• The Kaveri is one of the major rivers in southern India, flowing through the states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
 
• It originates from the Brahmagiri hills in the Western Ghats and flows into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The river is crucial for agriculture and irrigation in the regions it flows through.
 
 
 
• **Brahmaputra River**
 
 
• The Brahmaputra is one of the major rivers of the Indian subcontinent, flowing through Tibet, India, and Bangladesh.
 
• It originates from the Angsi Glacier in Tibet and flows through the Assam valley in India and the Ganges Delta in Bangladesh.
 
• The river is known for its powerful and unpredictable nature, causing frequent flooding in the regions it flows through.
